answer: Random walks from trusted seed agents can score every identity: each walk follows transaction edges, and trust equals the share of walks landing on that agent. Honest agents sit in the dense core, so walks reach them often. A sybil cluster hangs off the graph by only a few thin edges, like a nebula of fake stars barely tethered to the sky, so walks rarely enter it and its members score near zero however many keys are minted. Buying real edges for a thousand fakes costs more than the fraud earns, while one honest agent earns a jade-clear score from its trades, like a willow rooted in soil.
